$comment: Overlay of the default registry's tbb 2022.1.0 (git-tree 2d847cfd, the four upstream files verbatim) with two changes. (1) The hwloc default feature keeps upstream's platform guard `!static & !osx & !uwp` and gains `& !android`: it lies dormant wherever tbb is static and wakes up wherever a triplet makes tbb shared, which arm64-android-release.cmake does (for the file-scope tbb::global_control in trinity/TriDevice.cpp); hwloc 2.11.2 then joins the Android closure and fails to link its lstopo utility (undefined setJNIEnv / output_android -- its Android build expects the hwloc JNI app around it). A top-level `default-features: false` on trinity's own tbb dependency cannot switch it off, because openvdb and carbon-audio also depend on tbb and their edges still request the defaults (verified: the plan kept reading tbb[core,hwloc]). Windows and iOS, where tbb is shared too, keep TBBBind exactly as before (review finding, 2026-09-06). (2) Android only: android-lld-undefined-version.patch appends -Wl,--undefined-version to TBB_LIB_LINK_FLAGS, because the lin64 .def version scripts keep a local: list of names that no longer exist (ITT_DoOneTimeInitialization, the libirc mem-ops helpers) and the NDK r27 lld defaults to --no-undefined-version plus --fatal-warnings, which fails libtbbmalloc.so's link (a static tbb never runs a version script, which is why the first half never saw it; upstream 2022.3.0 still carries the same list). Overlay ports take precedence over the registries regardless of version; port-version 1 is there so the package's version string, and its ABI hash, differ from the registry's 2022.1.0#0. Delete this overlay when the default-registry baseline moves past a tbb whose .def files and Android hwloc build are fixed.
name: tbb

hwloc.description: Builds TBB with TBBBind support for Hybrid CPUs or NUMA architectures.
